page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.large is an x86_64 architecture instance belonging to the Shared server family. It is equipped with 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, supported by 32.0 GB of RAM. This provides a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio (8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU). The instance runs on a KVM hypervisor and includes CPU instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA. It does not provide attached local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results place the processing and memory performance of the ecs.e3.large primarily in the lower tiers. In computational metrics, it achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 955.0 and multi-core score of 2993.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 5197.9. Compute-intensive compression tasks also registered low throughput, with single-threaded gzip compression at 18.91 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 13.2 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 33.54 GB/sec, while large-block write bandwidth showed moderate throughput at 28.36 GB/sec.

In operational benchmarks, the instance completed Redis SET operations at 4.46 million operations per second and handled static web serving throughput at 3.08 GB/sec. PassMark database operations scored 1075.89, placing it in the bottom performance decile. Given the 32.0 GB memory footprint paired with modest compute throughput and lack of local storage, the instance functions as an entry-tier memory-expanded node suited for lightweight in-memory caching, low-traffic web applications, non-critical background services, and test environments where high memory density is needed without high compute demands.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.large is an x86_64 server instance featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, accompanied by 32.0 GB of system RAM. Configured with an expanded 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, it operates without local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates entry-level performance, logging a PassMark CPU score of 5197.9, a Geekbench multi-core score of 2993.0, and 4.46 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 33.54 GB/sec for uncached reads and 28.36 GB/sec for uncached writes. Due to its combination of high memory capacity relative to compute capacity, it is appropriately positioned for memory-reliant but computationally light workloads such as small in-memory caches, staging servers, and non-intensive internal applications.
